newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended sharply higher on Monday after EU finance ministers reached a landmark deal on the budget stability pact in Amsterdam.
But dealers said most of the gains had already been factored in and rollover activity during the last trading day for the long bond June contract prompted a large part of trade.
"I do not expect our (debt) market to move with high volume until the Amsterdam summit ends," a dealer at All Trading in Madrid said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended virtually unchanged.
The spread closed at 69 basis points, down from 70 basis points in early trade.
Earlier on Monday, the Bank of Spain left its key rate unchanged at 5.25 percent despite benign May inflation data which created scope for further monetary easing, dealers said.
But analysts said an official rate cut should come as soon as the next ten days.
"I guess it just delayed the move by eight days, because of the Amsterdam summit," said Henrik Lumholdt, chief economist at Bank of America in Madrid.
